survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This OECD country note summarizes indicators from Education at a Glance 2025 using the latest available reference years for Sweden. It does not provide an analysis-ready student micro-dataset or an explicit sampling/replicate-weighting specification in the note itself. The figures and rates are therefore best interpreted as already-processed OECD estimates based on the underlying survey designs (e.g., Survey of Adult Skills for literacy and unemployment/attainment indicators, and other OECD administrative/statistical sources for education participation and finance). For any re-analysis at micro level, analysts should consult the corresponding Education at a Glance 2025 Sources, Methodologies and Technical Notes and the OECD Handbook for Internationally Comparative Education Statistics to apply the correct complex survey weights and scaling/PV procedures used for each indicator.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This document is a descriptive country note that reports indicator results (shares, trends, and cross-country comparisons) rather than estimating models from student-level plausible values. Plausible Values are typically used for cognitive achievement scales in ILSA assessments, but this note does not present any PV-based modeling or PV-combining procedure. Missing-data handling is not described because the note does not report an original micro-data analysis pipeline; instead, it relies on OECD-compiled indicator outputs.

data.outcome_summary: Education at a Glance 2025 (Sweden country note) provides a descriptive overview of education system characteristics, with emphasis on tertiary education, using the latest available reference years. The note reports cross-generational educational attainment patterns, unemployment rates by educational attainment, and literacy proficiency distributions from the OECD Survey of Adult Skills (PIAAC), including trends across PIAAC Cycle 1 (2012–15) and Cycle 2 (2023). It also summarizes education participation and progression indicators (e.g., age-for-grade in lower secondary, entry routes into tertiary, gender composition of entrants, completion and dropout rates, and international student mobility) and education finance and workforce indicators (expenditure per student, funding shares, teacher shortages/qualification gaps, turnover, and instructional time/class size). Because it is not an original student-level modeling study, it does not specify PV handling, missing-data procedures, or ML model performance; instead, it directs readers to the OECD tables and technical notes for indicator construction and underlying methodology.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This extraction corresponds to an OECD descriptive country note rather than an empirical ML paper. As a result, there is no student-level analytic sample, no model estimation, and no reported ML algorithms or predictive targets; therefore fields such as total_students, per-country n_students, and main_findings are not applicable in the ML/ILSA predictive sense. The note’s methodological transparency is provided indirectly via references to the Education at a Glance 2025 tables and the Sources, Methodologies and Technical Notes, which contain the indicator-specific sampling, scaling, and data-processing details.
